Chapter 10: Embracing the Mystery—Living the Miracle
Picture this: it’s a quiet evening, years down the road. A couple sits together in the soft, fading light. The house is peaceful, the kids have grown up and moved on, and all those moments of struggle and celebration have become threads in the fabric of their shared life. They look at each other—not with the wide-eyed wonder they once had, but with a deep, steady affection that only comes from years of choosing each other, forgiving, and growing—side by side.
You know, most of us spend our lives searching for certainty. We want answers to all the big questions. But if marriage teaches us anything, it’s that some things aren’t meant to be solved. Some mysteries are simply meant to be lived. The unknown isn’t a puzzle to fix—it’s actually a gift to receive.
Think about it: marriage invites us to keep showing up, to keep loving, even when we don’t have it all figured out. There’s something beautiful being created, even when life feels uncertain.
For those who are willing to lean into that mystery, marriage turns into a real source of strength and joy. Sure, it’s not always easy. There are tough days, and sometimes the road gets bumpy. But honestly? It’s always worth it.
The true miracle isn’t about having a life without struggle—it’s about having a love that endures, no matter what.
